'''Ukita no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (浮田国造), also known as '''Ukita Kokuzō''', was the {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|es|Kuni no miyatsuko|ff|Kuni no miyatsuko|it|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|ko|국조 (일본)|simple|Kuni no miyatsuko|vi|Kuni no miyatsuko|zh|國造|qid=Q2483673|lt=Kuni no Miyatsuko}} who governed the ancient territory of [[Ukita Province]], corresponding to the eastern part of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|qid=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}}.

== Overview ==

=== Ancestry ===
According to the ''{{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}'' ("Records of Ancient Matters"), the office of Ukita no Kuni no Miyatsuko was established during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|en|Emperor Seimu|qid=Q316672|lt=Emperor Seimu}}, appointing '''{{ill|Kagawaki|ja|賀我別王}}''', a fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, as the first ruler of the region.

=== Clan ===
The clan name was '''{{ill|Kibiya clan|ja|吉弥侯部}}''' (read "Kimikobe Uji"). They were kin to the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|ja|上毛野氏}}, {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, and other related clans such as the {{ill|Harima Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|針間鴨国造|qid=Q108487215}}. In the first year of {{ill|Jingo-keiun|en|Jingo-keiun|qid=Q1373049|lt=Jingō-keiun}} (767 CE), on {{nihongo|July 19|7月19日}}, Kimikobe Ishimaro (吉弥侯部石麻呂), a resident of {{ill|Uda district|ja|宇多郡|qid=Q11449246}}, was granted the surname of "Kamitsukeno Mutsu no Kimi" (上毛野陸奥公).

== Territory ==

=== Domain ===
The Ukita no Kuni no Miyatsuko governed the region known as "Ukita Province," which later became part of {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|qid=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}}. The domain encompassed areas in {{ill|Uda district|ja|宇多郡|qid=Q11449246}} and {{ill|Q16769301|ja|行方郡|qid=Q16769301}}, corresponding to modern {{ill|Sōma, Fukushima|en|Sōma, Fukushima|qid=Q696456|lt=Sōma, Fukushima}}, {{ill|Minamisōma|en|Minamisōma|qid=Q642094|lt=Minamisōma}}, and parts of {{ill|Shinchi, Fukushima|en|Shinchi, Fukushima|qid=Q1205416|lt=Shinchi, Fukushima}} and {{ill|Iitate, Fukushima|en|Iitate, Fukushima|qid=Q674500|lt=Iitate, Fukushima}} in Fukushima Prefecture. Neighboring domains at the time included the {{ill|Q85876227|ja|伊久国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iku no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q85876227}} to the northwest and the {{ill|Someha no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|染羽国造}} to the south.

During the reforms following the {{ill|Taika Reform|en|Taika Reform|qid=Q570140|lt=Taika Reforms}}, the regions were restructured, with the Uda River valley forming Uda District and the Nitta River valley forming Nakama District.<ref>Hirakawa Minami, ''Ancient History of the Tōhoku "Kaido,"'' Iwanami Shoten, 2012, p. 122.</ref>

== Religious Significance ==

=== Clan Shrine ===
The sole {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} and {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin-taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q9610964}} in {{ill|Uda district|ja|宇多郡|qid=Q11449246}} is the '''{{ill|Kobimine Shrine|ja|子眉嶺神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Komidake Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11447922}}''', believed to be associated with the Ukita no Kuni no Miyatsuko.

=== Kofuns ===

* '''{{ill|Sakurai Kofun|en|Sakurai Kofun|qid=Q11537784|lt=Sakurai Kofun}}'''
: Located in {{ill|Minamisōma|en|Minamisōma|qid=Q642094|lt=Minamisōma}}, Fukushima Prefecture, this keyhole-shaped tumulus (全長74メートル) dates to the late 4th or early 5th century. It is considered the possible burial site of {{ill|Kagawake|ja|鹿我別|qid=Q17226573}}, the clan's progenitor.<ref>Hōga Toshio, "[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/hitori/kimikobe1.htm Genealogy of the Kimikobe-surnamed Madara Clan]," 2016.</ref>

* '''{{ill|Mano Kofun Cluster|en|Mano Kofun Cluster|qid=Q11583561|lt=Mano Kofungun}}'''
: Also located in Minamisōma, this large cluster of Kofuns from the late Kofun period includes two keyhole-shaped tumuli and numerous circular mounds.

'''Ukita no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (''ukita no kuni no miyatsuko'', ''ukita kokuzō'') was a {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} who ruled [[#Territory|Ukita Province]] (eastern {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}}).

== Overview ==
=== Ancestry ===
* According to the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'', during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ja|成務天皇|lt=Emperor Seimu}}, '''{{ill|Kaga-Wake|ja|鹿我別|lt=Kaga-Wake-no-Ōkimi}}''', 5th-generation descendant of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, was appointed kuni no miyatsuko.

=== Clan ===
'''{{ill|Kimikobe clan|ja|吉弥侯部|lt=Kimikobe clan}}''' (''kimikobe-uji''; {{ill|kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane}} unknown), kin to the {{ill|Kamitsukenu clan|ja|上毛野氏}}, {{ill|Shimotsukenu clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, and {{ill|Harima-Kamo no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|針間鴨国造}}. On the [[July 19|19th day of the 7th month]] of {{ill|Jingo-keiun|ja|神護景雲}} 1 ([[767]]), Kimikobe-no-Ishimaro, a Ge-shō-rokui-jō, Kun-jūtō of {{ill|Uda District|ja|宇多郡}}, was granted the surname '''Kamitsukenu-Mutsu-{{ill|Kimi (kabane)|ja|キミ (カバネ)|lt=Kimi}}'''.

== Base ==
=== Territory ===
The territory of the kuni no miyatsuko was the region then called '''Ukita Province''', corresponding to the later {{ill|ritsuryō province|ja|律令国}} of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}} '''{{ill|Uda District|ja|宇多郡}}''' and '''{{ill|Namekata District, Fukushima|ja|行方郡 (福島県)|lt=Namekata District}}''', equivalent to present-day {{ill|Sōma, Fukushima|ja|相馬市|lt=Sōma City}}, {{ill|Minamisōma, Fukushima|ja|南相馬市|lt=Minamisōma City}}, {{ill|Shinchi, Fukushima|ja|新地町|lt=Shinchi Town}} in {{ill|Sōma District, Fukushima|ja|相馬郡|lt=Sōma District}}, and {{ill|Iitate, Fukushima|ja|飯舘村|lt=Iitate Village}} in the same district. Contemporary with the establishment of the Ukita no Kuni no Miyatsuko, the {{ill|Iku no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|伊久国造}} ({{ill|Igu District|ja|伊具郡}}) was placed to the northwest, and the {{ill|Somewa no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|染羽国造}} ({{ill|Shineha District|ja|標葉郡}}) to the south.

After the {{ill|Taika Reform|ja|大化の改新}}, when the {{ill|hyō system|ja|評|lt=hyō system}} was implemented nationwide, there is a theory that the {{ill|Uda River|ja|宇多川}} basin became Uda-hyō, and the {{ill|Nitta River|ja|新田川}} basin became Namekata-hyō<ref>{{ill|Hirakawa Minami|ja|平川南}}, ''Tōhoku "Kaidō" no Kodaishi'', {{ill|Iwanami Shoten|ja|岩波書店}}, 2012, p. 122.</ref>.

== Tutelary Shrine ==
'''{{ill|Komi-ne Shrine|ja|子眉嶺神社}}''', the sole {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} of {{ill|Uda District|ja|宇多郡}} and a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}}.

=== Tombs ===
*'''{{ill|Sakurai Kofun|ja|桜井古墳}}''' (''sakurai-kofun'')
*:A 74 m long {{ill|keyhole-rectangle kofun|ja|前方後方墳}} in {{ill|Minamisōma, Fukushima|ja|南相馬市|lt=Minamisōma City}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, constructed in the late {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀}} to the early {{ill|5th century|ja|5世紀}}. Based on its location and construction date, there is a theory that it is the tomb of {{ill|Kaga-Wake-no-Mikoto|ja|鹿我別|lt=Kaga-Wake-no-Mikoto}}, the first ancestor of the Ukita no Kuni no Miyatsuko<ref>{{ill|Hōga Toshio|ja|宝賀寿男}}, "[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/hitori/kimikobe1.htm The Genealogy of the Madaramoku Clan of the Kimikobe Kabane]," ''Koju Kinobōma'', 2016.</ref>.
*'''{{ill|Mano Kofun Group|ja|真野古墳群}}''' (''mano-kofun-gun'')
*:A large-scale late {{ill|Kofun period|af|Kofun-tydperk|ar|فترة كوفون|az|Kofun dövrü|be|Кафун|bg|Кофун|bn|কোফুন যুগ|ca|Període Kofun|cs|Období Kofun|de|Kofun-Zeit|eo|Kofun-epoko|es|Período Kofun|eu|Kofun aroa|fa|دوره کوفون|fi|Kofun-kausi|fr|Période Kofun|he|תקופת קופון|hr|Razdoblje Kofun|hu|Kofun-kor|id|Zaman Kofun|it|Periodo Kofun|ja|古墳時代|ko|고훈 시대|lt|Kofun laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Kofun|nl|Kofunperiode|pl|Kofun (okres)|pt|Período Kofun|ro|Perioada Kofun|ru|Период Кофун|sh|Kofunski period|simple|Kofun period|sk|Obdobie Kofun|sl|Obdobje Kofun|sr|Кофун период|sv|Kofunperioden|th|ยุคโคฟุง|tl|Panahong Kofun|tr|Kofun Dönemi|uk|Період Кофун|vi|Thời kỳ Kofun|wuu|古坟时代|zh|古坟时代|zh_min_nan|Kohun sî-tāi|zh_yue|古墳時代|qid=Q459939}} {{ill|kofun group|ja|古墳群}} in Minamisōma City, Fukushima Prefecture, composed of 2 {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} and numerous {{ill|round kofun|ja|円墳}}.
